main_body: Leafy tree canopy (about 30 rows tall) on a thin brown trunk with a small dark grass base patch
top_band: none: the canopy is a rounded organic mass; the column scan shows leaf-clump tones (L 60-170) with no flat top surface or front-edge step
evidence: The kind is organic (tree). The canopy is a rounded foliage blob with light clumps at the upper right and darker clumps below, so it reads as volume lit from above, not as a flat front elevation. There is no rectangular top, lid or rim to judge, and no receding side face. The trunk and its base patch sit below the canopy. As an organic object the 3/4 contract (top plus front face) does not apply in a strict sense, and nothing in it contradicts the 3/4 view.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references, so it is far less rich. It has five green steps (dark outline green, mid greens, light, highlight) with dithered clumps and no 5x5 flat fills, and the dark edge pixels are tinted dark green (0% neutral). Even so, the canopy is a smooth blob of blocky patches with no individual leaf clusters, no branches showing through and only a plain straight trunk with no roots or flare. The references show far more varied leaf clumps, bark texture and root detail. Next to them this piece looks thinner and flatter, so it fails.
